Celebrations of this holiday in the city of Sirsi feature a man dressed as a sword-wielding monster clad in peacock feathers, who dances to the rhythms of the tamte drum.
In some places, men celebrate this holiday by making human pyramids in an attempt to reach a pot of butter.
Among the legends associated with this holiday are the murder of a she-demon with poisonous breast milk and the love between Rati and Kama.
The main event of this holiday occurs on a full moon during the month of Phalguna.

This holiday recalls how a demon king, immune to both astra and shastra, was killed by the claws of the half-lion Narasimha. Bonfires set on the eve of this holiday commemorate the saving of the demon king’s son, Prahlad.
Prahlada survived on a pyre while this holiday’s namesake demoness burned to death due to her devotion to Vishnu.
Vishnu's avatar Krishna plays pranks on the gopis, who react by throwing abir, this holiday’s famed colored powder.
During this holiday, one might find people filling water balloons and water guns with pigments and attempting to spray each other.
